plainMeaning: Source Path records where source/imported material came from. A locator on current managed media is not automatically that fact.
A concrete native import route is the applicable master’s own _IMPORTSETTING attribute list, then its _SRCFILE object reference to a file locator.

Another concrete route is that owner’s own _USER list and its exact UNC Path text attribute. Despite the label, a native Mac writer stores its full Mac-encoded source path there; the label alone does not prove a Windows network path.
Native helpers can follow explicit source-clip links to descriptors belonging to source-file material; they do not need to use every arbitrary locator in the MDB.

Encoding preference and path-variant preference are different decisions. UTF8 and legacy spellings, canonical paths, POSIX paths and UNC variants may differ without referring to different original files.

bellaImplicationsNotNewApproval: Use an explicit owner/path-route priority table. Selected-master own _IMPORTSETTING._SRCFILE and own _USER.UNC Path are supported native routes; other owner/source-descriptor fallbacks require an agreed bounded relationship rule.
Keep one full recorded source path or supported URL and a compact availability/provenance status. Do not add a Source Filename column or strip its basename by assumption.

Within a chosen locator prefer its supported knownUTF8 canonical representation, then its separately stored known legacy fallback under approved MacRoman scope. A POSIX or UNC variant is not higher quality merely from its name.

Do not pool all path strings and demand equality. Named UTF8 and legacy text, canonical/POSIX representation, and native/UNC variants can legitimately differ. Choose by established property/extension role, not equality or object order.
Current physical media path remains filesystem Location. Never use an arbitrary managed-media descriptor locator to fill original Source Path simply because it is nonempty.
Do not introduce filesystem existence checks, alias resolution, volume search, mount attempts, relinking, or writes to repair _SRCFILE. Missing metadata leaves the physical row intact.
limits: Static code evidence describes these native routes, not every MDB producer/version or every Media Composer UI presentation.
No actualMDBcounts claimed here; parent/data agent owns current raw corpus probes and semantic variant examples.
Fresh inspected main functions use same main hash as OriginalBin review; engine hashes match Project/text reviews.
No proof all generic path-like names are UTF8 or MacRoman; this receipt identifies specific named/typed contracts under approved scope.

Some native helpers choose first found/first nonempty and can mutate in-memory state; Bella can deliberately use safer independent rules rather than copy those behaviors.

supersededExtractionProposal.meaning: One full recorded source/import path or supported URL, including any filename present. It need not exist today and is not necessarily earliest camera original. Location remains separate.
supersededExtractionProposal.owner: Already selected master for direct import paths, even if its Clip Name is blank. Never select a different master for a path.
routeOrder: Selected master own exact _IMPORTSETTING Kind3 -> ATTR -> exact _SRCFILE Kind3 -> supported file locator
If no usable import path: selected master own exact _USER Kind3 -> ATTR -> exact UNC Path supported text
If still unavailable: physical file own supported local components SourceID -> full-ID-qualified immediate source MobType3 -> typed MDES:MobKind=5 descriptor -> proven MACL locator

Separate readable OMFI:FL:POSIXPathName under approved MacRoman legacy scope
Separate readable OMFI:FL:PathName under approved MacRoman legacy scope
supersededExtractionProposal.variantQualification: Legacy POSIX before legacy canonical is a proposed Bella display choice, not universal native state/OS behavior. Preserve chosen recorded spelling without filesystem/HFS reconstruction. Distinguish known canonical and UNC roles where layout provides them; unresolved same-priority Unicode variants leave field unavailable rather than choosing by order.
supersededExtractionProposal.encoding: Approved strict known UTF8 then separate readable MacRoman fallback. POSIXPathName is not declared UTF8 by its label. Known UNC Path Kind2 uses MacRoman; supported marker-bearing text Kind4 uses its known UTF8 layout. Never reinterpret malformed Unicode as legacy.
supersededExtractionProposal.fallbackScope: Immediate file-to-source relationship only; no recursive original-source ancestry search in release one. Require correct catalogue/role, full identity, readable descriptor kind5 and proven locator text contract. Unavailable master may still permit an independently qualified file/source fact; never replace the supplied master ID.
supersededExtractionProposal.conflict: Same-priority qualified candidates must provide one unambiguous value or exact agreement. Unresolved relationships or conflicting same-priority candidates leave MDB Source Path unavailable. A usable higher-priority path need not equal lower-priority variants/routes. No basename or filesystem-equivalence heuristic.
supersededExtractionProposal.excluded: No arbitrary MSML managed-media locator, tape(kind2) descriptor path, Audio/Video container tag, archived attribute, or unproven URLL-only storage projection. Other locator/layout support remains separately reviewable.
supersededExtractionProposal.empty: Advance along this bounded order for absent/blank/unusable text; if exhausted leave Source Path blank and keep physical file. Missing metadata is not proof no original source ever existed.
supersededExtractionProposal.retention: One selected full path/URL and compact availability/owner/route status. Preserve nonblank spelling, separators and percent escapes. No Source Filename, basename, alternative spellings, second URI-decoded value or lasting raw graph.
supersededExtractionProposal.passive: No source-file opening/existence checks, alias resolution, volume/network/mount searches, relinking, repair writes, guessed current paths or appended filenames.
